newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk rights group sees November rise in violations.
newsitem.headline: Turk rights group sees November rise in violations.

text.p: A Turkish rights group said on Friday that figures for November showed human rights violations in Turkey had increased from a year earlier despite government pledges to improve its record.
"Only comparing figures of November 1995 and November 1996 one can see rights violations have not fallen, but increased," Avni Kalkan of the Human Rights Association (IHD), told Reuters.

An IHD report showed 11 people died in mysterious killings in November 1996 compared with three in the year earlier period. Claims of torture were made by 17 people in November this year, up from 12 the previous year.
The number of people who died after being taken into custody fell to eight from 16 a year earlier, but Kalkan said the trend in violations was upwards.
The November report showed 142 intellectuals, writers and journalists were in prison for their speeches and writings last month, up from 133 in November 1995.
Turkey has faced sharp criticism for its right record from Western countries and international rights organizations.

There was also an increase in the number of people killed in the 12-year-old struggle between Kurdish separatists and security forces to 355 in November from 276 a year earlier. More than 21,000 people have died since the rebel Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) began its fight for autonomy or independence in southeastern Turkey in 1984.
Kalkan doubted the government would improve the rights situation despite a pledge by Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller and a draft law shortening the period of police detention for suspects.
"In my opinion there will not be much improvement, because these reforms are just aimed at creating a positive appearance in the eyes of the West," he said.
